analysis.description: This paper critiques the current approaches to out-of-distribution (OOD) detection in machine learning, particularly in object recognition contexts. It argues for benchmarks that focus on semantic anomalies rather than non-semantic distributional shifts. The paper proposes using multi-task learning to improve semantic anomaly detection by incorporating auxiliary objectives that encourage semantic representation, thereby enhancing generalization and anomaly detection capabilities in neural networks.

name.justification: CIFAR-10 is a key dataset used for evaluating the proposed benchmarks in the paper.
name.quote: For a choice of dataset, for example MNIST, train as many versions of classifiers as there are classes, holding out one class every time. At evaluation time, score the ability of being able to detect the held out class as anomalous. This is a setup more clearly related to the task of being able to detect semantic anomalies, holding dataset-bias factors invariant to a significantly greater extent. In this paper, we shall explore this setting with CIFAR-10 and STL-10, and recommend this as the default benchmark for evaluating anomaly detection in the context of object recognition.
